sam.k: Heads upwent to Riverwalk Immediate Care today and they said the insurer system couldn't validate my plan. I only had the insurer app screenshot on my phone. They said no card = can't bill. Ended up paying $98. Any tips to get reimbursed?

ana (People Ops): Sorry that happened, @sam.k. Short checklist: 1) keep the itemized charge/receipt (must include service date, CPT or description, total, provider name). 2) pull the digital ID PDF from the insurer portal (screenshot sometimes works but PDF is better). 3) send claim to insurer and cc benefits@redwood.com.

sam.k: I have a generic receipt that just says "urgent care visit" and a charge total. No CPT codes. Will that be enough?

ryan-broker: It might be, but insurer often asks for an itemized bill. Call the clinic billing office and request an itemized statement or a UB-04/HCFA style breakdown. Ask them to include their NPI and tax ID if possible.

sam.k: Clinic said they don't have my member & group in their system even though the plan shows as active on the insurer app. They suggested I call insurer to get an authorization code.

ana (People Ops): Usually no pre-auth for urgent care, but directory mismatches happen. Two parallel paths: (A) submit a claim for reimbursement as an out-of-pocket claim with the receipt, (B) have the clinic resubmit once they accept the plan. We can help chase the insurer/broker if needed.

insurer-bot: Digital ID ready for member 987654321: https://portal.insurer/ids/987654321.pdf :file_folder:  (valid through 2027-03-01)

ryan-broker: If insurer initially denies because provider couldn't be verified, you can file a provider-directory dispute. That often triggers reprocessing if provider is actually in-network. We'll open the dispute once benefits@redwood.com gives the green light.

sam.k: Ok I'll request the itemized bill from the clinic. If they refuse, is there a standard form insurer accepts for out-of-pocket claims?

ana (People Ops): Yes, most insurers have a member claim form (PDF) on their site. If the receipt lacks CPTs, attach a clinic note or the front-desk signed receipt plus a cover letter explaining the service. Use this quick template for the claim email:

```
To: claims@portal.insurer
Subject: Member claim submission  Member ID 987654321  urgent care 2026-07-10
Body: Please find attached receipt for urgent care visit on 2026-07-10 for Sam K. Member Name: Sam K, Member ID: 987654321, Group: RW-00011. Provider: Riverwalk Immediate Care. Please advise on processing and reimbursement steps.
Attachments: receipt.pdf, digital_id.pdf, clinic_itemized_request.pdf
```

ryan-broker: Pro-tip: include the clinic NPI or Tax ID if they provide it. Also request an "itemized statement" rather than just a payment receipt.

sam.k: Sent the clinic a request for an itemized statement; also submitted the claim to claims@portal.insurer and cc'd benefits@redwood.com. Thanks for the quick responses.

ana (People Ops): Thanks @sam.k. I've noted this with our broker and will follow up if the claim stalls. Expect an insurer acknowledgment within 5-10 business days, EOB in 2-4 weeks typically. If denied, we'll submit an appeal; please keep the receipts and any phone call notes (date/time and rep name).

sam.k: Good to know. One last Q: how do I get a physical card? The app is fine but some places still ask.

insurer-bot: Physical ID cards can be requested via member portal > Account Settings > Request Card. Expedited mailing available in some regions.

ryan-broker: If you want, ping me and I'll request an expedited paper card on your behalf through the broker channel.

sam.k: Appreciate it  I'll take the expedited card if clinic issues persist.

ana (People Ops): Closing loop: benefits@redwood.com has the claim and we'll escalate if insurer doesn't process within the expected timeframe. Feel free to DM with updates. :spiral_calendar:
